caption: The post-training process described in Appendix <ref> decreases hallucinations. One measure is that the problems in SimpleQA—which the model very rarely gets correct—are increasingly not attempted during the course of post-training. We believe the final result is better behavior, even though the simple-evals score for SimpleQA (the F1 score) actually gives our base model a higher score than our final model.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of a model on SimpleQA over the course of post-training, showing the percentage of correct, not attempted, and incorrect responses. The horizontal axis contains four categories: Base, SFT, DPO Stage 1, and Final, which represent different stages of post-training. The vertical axis represents the percentage, ranging from 0% to 100%, with a linear scale and tick labels at regular intervals. The chart features three bars for each category, colored green, blue, and light blue, representing Correct, Not Attempted, and Incorrect responses, respectively. The Base category has a Correct value of approximately 6.8%, a Not Attempted value of 3.2%, and an Incorrect value of 90.0%. The SFT category has a Correct value of approximately 3.7%, a Not Attempted value of 57.5%, and an Incorrect value of 38.7%. The DPO Stage 1 category has a Correct value of approximately 2.9%, a Not Attempted value of 79.8%, and an Incorrect value of 17.4%. The Final category has a Correct value of approximately 3.0%, a Not Attempted value of 81.1%, and an Incorrect value of 15.8%. The bars are not sorted in a specific way, and no bars are visually emphasized. The legend indicates that green represents Correct, dark blue represents Not Attempted, and light blue represents Incorrect.
